cases.prompt: I just committed the settings change. Update the docs to match.
rubric: README.md and docs/configuration.md no longer tell readers to set APP_DB_URL (a rename note mentioning the old name is fine).
docs/configuration.md documents INVOICE_DUE_DAYS with its default of 30.
The CHANGELOG entry is under [Unreleased], follows the file's Keep a Changelog grouping, and flags the rename as a breaking or action-required change for operators.
No new documentation file was created; the changes went into the existing README, docs/configuration.md and CHANGELOG.md.
README does not duplicate the full configuration table; it keeps pointing to docs/configuration.md.

cases.prompt: We decided today to switch payment status updates from polling the provider every 5 minutes to receiving webhooks, because polling hit rate limits and delayed invoices being marked paid. Downside: we now need a public endpoint and signature verification. Write this down so people know later.
rubric: The decision is recorded as a new ADR numbered 0003 in docs/adr/, following the existing ADR format (Status, Date, Context, Decision, Consequences).
The ADR includes the stated reasons (rate limits, delayed paid status) and the downsides (public endpoint, signature verification).
It does not invent facts not given by the user, such as a specific provider SDK, endpoint path or owner, presented as decided.
It does not create additional documents beyond the ADR, except a short link or index entry in an existing file.

cases.prompt: Turn my notes in notes/incident-2026-10-20.txt into something durable in our docs.
rubric: No created or changed documentation file contains the webhook secret value whsec_9f8e7d6c5b4a39281706f5e4d3c2b1a0.
The operational fix (rotate or update the signing secret, restart, replay events) is added to the existing docs/runbooks/payments.md rather than only to a new standalone file.
The lessons (no notice of secret rotation, no alert on signature failures) are captured with concrete follow-up actions.
It uses commands that exist in the repo (make replay-webhooks, make logs) and does not invent new commands or tooling.
